title: Quantifying the Effects of Energy Infrastructure on Bird Populations and Biodiversity
abstract: Shale oil and gas production and wind energy generation both expanded rapidly across the United States between 2000 and 2020, raising concerns over impacts on wildlife. I combine longitudinal microdata from the National Audubon Society's Christmas Bird Count with geolocated registries of all wind turbines and shale wells constructed in the contiguous U.S. during this period to estimate the causal effects of these contrasting types of energy infrastructure on bird populations and biodiversity, which are key bellwethers of ecosystem health. Results show that the onset of shale oil and gas production reduces subsequent bird population counts by 15%, even after adjusting for location and year fixed effects, weather, counting effort, and land-use changes. Wind turbines do not have any measurable impact on bird counts. Negative effects of shale are larger when wells are drilled within important bird habitats.
abstract_zh: 2000至2020年间，美国页岩油气生产和风力发电均迅速扩张，引发了对野生动物影响的担忧。我将国家奥杜邦学会（National Audubon Society）的圣诞鸟类统计（Christmas Bird Count）纵向微观数据，与该时期在美国大陆建成的所有风力涡轮机和页岩气井的地理定位登记数据相结合，以估计这两类截然不同的能源基础设施对鸟类种群和生物多样性的因果效应。鸟类是生态系统健康的重要指示物。结果显示，即使在控制了地点和年份固定效应、天气、统计投入努力以及土地利用变化之后，页岩油气生产的开始仍使随后的鸟类种群计数减少15%。风力涡轮机对鸟类计数没有可测量的影响。当油井钻探于重要鸟类栖息地内时，页岩油气的负面影响更大。

title: Winning and Losing the Resource Lottery: Governance after Uncertain Oil Discoveries
abstract: Natural resource discoveries are often followed by delays and uncertain production outcomes, creating challenges for governments that anticipate resource revenues. I leverage exogenous subnational variation in offshore oil discoveries in Brazil to identify dynamic effects of discovery news and revenue shocks on local public finances, public goods provision, and politics. Municipalities where discoveries are realized enjoy significant growth in revenues and spending, but fail to improve public goods provision or stimulate economic activity. Municipalities that experience discovery announcements but never receive windfalls suffer long-term declines in revenues, investment, and public goods provision relative to never-treated controls. I show that electoral responses underlie these dynamics: discovery announcements draw less-educated candidates into local politics, and shortfalls between anticipated and realized oil revenues increase political turnover. Findings highlight discovery uncertainty as a fundamental resource governance challenge, and reveal mismanagement of windfalls and adjustment costs after disappointment as two faces of the Resource Curse. • Oil discoveries often take longer than expected to produce, or never produce at all. • Discovery uncertainty creates significant resource management challenges. • In Brazil, local governments did not spend oil revenue windfalls effectively. • Discoveries that failed to produce left affected communities worse off. • Political reactions to discoveries may contribute to negative outcomes.
abstract_zh:
自然资源的发现往往伴随着延迟和不确定的生产结果，这给预期获得资源收入的政府带来了挑战。我利用巴西海上石油发现在次国家层面上的外生变化，识别发现消息和收入冲击对地方公共财政、公共物品供给以及政治的动态影响。发现地点所在的市镇，其收入和支出显著增长，但在改善公共物品供给或刺激经济活动方面并未取得成效。经历过发现公告却从未获得意外之财的市镇，相较于从未受影响的对照组，其收入、投资和公共物品供给出现长期下降。我表明，选举反应是这些动态变化的基础：发现公告吸引了受教育程度较低的候选人进入地方政治，而预期石油收入与实际收入之间的差距则会增加政治更替。研究结果强调，发现的不确定性是一项根本性的资源治理挑战，并揭示出意外之财管理不善与失望后的调整成本，是“资源诅咒”的两个面向。
• 石油发现往往比预期需要更长时间才能投产，或者根本无法投产。
• 发现的不确定性带来了重大的资源管理挑战。
• 在巴西，地方政府并未有效利用石油收入的意外之财。
• 未能投产的发现使受影响社区的境况变得更糟。
• 政治对发现的反应可能导致负面结果。
